_comment: Functions the original build did NOT compile with the default toolchain.
tools/agbcc/bin/ holds two compilers. The Makefile defined CC1_OLD for
old_agbcc from the start and never referenced it; wave 10 found out why it
is there. The sound and flash libraries came out of the SDK prebuilt with
their own settings and were dropped into the game's build, which is the
same layout every other GBA tree has.
This file is the single source of truth for that. tools/agbenv.py applies
it so trymatch.py and compile_probe judge a candidate the way the ROM was
actually built, and tools/gen_overrides_mk.py turns it into target-specific
make variables. Both must agree: an override known only to the build makes
every later wave re-attempt an already-solved function and conclude it
cannot be matched.
An entry needs the same standard of evidence as data/asm-resident.json --
a byte-for-byte match under the named configuration, and a note on what the
default configuration does differently. 'It matched when I changed a flag'
with no mechanism is how a real bug gets papered over.
Blast radius, measured by recompiling all 520 promoted files both ways:
old_agbcc changes 100 of them, dropping -fforce-addr changes 17. Neither
is a candidate for a global change. Per-file it costs nothing -- no
promoted file between 0x0806F710 and 0x080745C0 differs under old_agbcc,
and none above 0x08063A3C differs without -fforce-addr.
CONSTRAINT: an overridden function must sit in a .c file of its own. The
build applies flags per object, so a shared file would silently recompile
its neighbours with the wrong toolchain. tools/gen_overrides_mk.py fails
loudly rather than emitting a rule that would do that.
WAVE 38 (W38-A) -- DISCRIMINATOR, measured on the five MPlay*Control entry
points at 0x08071420..0x080715F8. The wave brief predicted all five would
need old_agbcc. They do not, and the split is clean:
match under BOTH compilers  sub_08071420 sub_08071488 sub_080714FC
need old_agbcc              sub_08071584 sub_080715F8
These five are the same skeleton -- ident guard, ident+1, walk tracks[] on a
0x50 stride testing trackBits, restore ident -- and differ only in the loop
body. The two that need the override are EXACTLY the two whose loop body
contains a CALL (both to sub_08071564/ClearModM); the three that do not are
exactly the three whose body is pure stores. So the axis is not `m4a`, not
the file, and not the skeleton: it is a call inside a loop body, which is
where r0 is simultaneously the argument register and the only free scratch,
and that is the one place the two allocators diverge. Both misses were
94.8% with the SIZE ALREADY EXACT -- register choice and instruction order,
never an instruction count.
Consequence for future waves, and it cuts BOTH ways. Verified by adding
throwaway entries for the three and re-running try_match: all three ALSO
match byte-for-byte under old_agbcc. So across all five, old_agbcc matches
5/5 and default agbcc matches 3/5 -- old_agbcc is a strict superset here.
Defaulting the 0x0806F710-0x080745C0 region to old_agbcc is therefore SAFE
(it agrees with the existing note that no promoted file in that range
differs under it) and is the better first guess for anything new there.
But the three entries were still REMOVED rather than kept: an override that
changes no bytes is unfalsifiable, it makes the file stop being evidence,
and gen_overrides_mk.py's one-function-per-.c constraint would force three
needless file splits. Keep entries only where the default is measurably
wrong. If you are matching in this region and land at 90-99% with the size
exact, try old_agbcc BEFORE touching the C -- but do not assume you need it.

sub_0805D438.reason: AI unit-list step. Built with -O2 -fno-gcse: the draft is byte-for-byte identical to the ROM under that configuration, relocations included, and 28 bytes too long under the default. With gcse on, its partial-redundancy pass merges the literal-pool address loads of gUnknown_030046B0, gUnknown_030040D8 and gUnknown_030046C0 across the half after the call, leaving three pool words the ROM does not have. No source construct reproduces that: empty `asm("" ::: "memory")` barriers at one point, two points and after every statement give +28, +24 and +32 bytes, because a memory clobber cannot reach register-level address computations. flag_probe bounds a -fno-gcse file to sub_0805D338..sub_0805D438, and sub_0805D344 in that window provably needs gcse (its whole sort half is byte-exact with gcse on and loses its frame and both spills with it off), so the file carrying this flag holds this function alone. Neighbours sub_0805D2A0, sub_0805D5EC and sub_0805D648 all need gcse.

sub_0808B1BC.reason: Flash library, 292 bytes. Parked at 8.2% under the DEFAULT -O2 configuration, which is the wrong one for this block; W60-I closed it at -O1 in one session. Wave 60 (orchestrator + W60-I). See the nine sibling entries for the measurement that established the flash library is -O1: nine byte-for-byte matches across 0x0808A3DC-0x0808B91C with no source change. This one needed source work on top of the flag, which is why it is credited to the agent and not to the sweep. NOT uniformly true across the span -- sub_0808AAF4, sub_0808AC7C and sub_0808B91C get LONGER under -O1, so each function still needs its own verdict.

sub_0808AAF4.reason: Flash library ReadFlashId, 152 bytes. Wave 95 (W95-F). Matched by transplanting pret's ReadFlashId (pokeemerald src/agb_flash.c, with its DELAY() macro; this ROM writes 0xF0 once in the exit sequence where pret writes it twice). Byte-exact under -O1 with or without -fforce-addr, the flash block's configuration (see sub_0808AB8C); the default -O2 configuration gives 26.3%. The wave 88/93 notes that this function is '-O2 by exception' and 'longer at -O1' were measured on a hand-written goto draft whose shape was the residual.

sub_0808AB8C.reason: Flash library, 148 bytes. Parked before this wave. Wave 60 (orchestrator). THE FLASH LIBRARY IS -O1, and this is the first direct measurement of it. data/compiler-overrides.json's own header already said so in passing -- 'the m4a library is old_agbcc at -O2 while the flash library is -O1, and they are different configurations' -- but that sentence was written as an aside while ruling -O1 OUT for an m4a function, no entry ever used it, and every function in 0x0808A3DC-0x0808B91C was parked against the SOURCE axis instead. Probing all 18 unmatched non-asm-resident functions in that span with -O2 removed and -O1 added produced NINE byte-for-byte matches with not one character of C changed, and moved four more a long way (sub_0808B1BC 8.2%->98.3% at 5 of 292 bytes, sub_0808AF00 and sub_0808AF74 both ->92.2%, sub_0808AE54 ->87.9%). The residuals the default configuration left behind were register-allocation shaped -- two globals exchanging r5/r6, `ands` where the ROM has `adds` -- which is what a different optimisation level looks like, not what a wrong source looks like. Same lesson as this wave's m4a sweep: a whole block parked on the source axis when the axis was the toolchain. Each of the nine is its own single-function split unit, so gen_overrides_mk.py's one-function-per-.c constraint is satisfied with no file split. NOT uniformly true across the span: sub_0808AAF4, sub_0808AC7C and sub_0808B91C all get LONGER under -O1 (+8/+4/+8 bytes), so -O1 is not a blanket answer for the block and each function still needs its own verdict.

sub_080705AC.reason: m4a m4aMPlayAllStop. Wave 60 (orchestrator). NOT an independent measurement -- this function matches under DEFAULT agbcc too, and it is what W60-B closed by correcting gNumMusicPlayers from 9 to 11 in aw2bhr.lds and teaching relocs_equivalent() about absolute symbols. It is here purely for FILE CONSISTENCY: COMPILER FLAGS APPLY TO THE WHOLE OBJECT FILE, and promote.py merged it into src/decomp/c_08070478.c alongside the five m4aSongNum* functions that genuinely require old_agbcc. The split build refuses a file whose members carry different overrides, so the choice was to split the file or make the whole file old_agbcc. Verified by exit status that this function is byte-identical under old_agbcc as well, so the file is consistent and nothing is lost -- exactly the same situation as sub_08070B34 and sub_08070C90 above. IF c_08070478.c IS EVER SPLIT INTO SEPARATE FILES, this entry can be deleted; it is a file-consistency entry, not a finding.

sub_08070478.reason: m4aSongNumStart. Parked at 88.6%/44 bytes. Wave 60 (orchestrator). The five m4aSongNum* entry points at 0x08070478-0x080705AC. ALL FIVE were parked in wave 32 with the IDENTICAL residual, size already exact: the ROM keeps &gUnknown_08242308 (the mplay table) in r2 and song->ms in r3, and every candidate under default agbcc produces them the other way round. Instruction stream, literal-pool order and size were otherwise the ROM's in each case. Wave 32 then measured the gcc-2.9 local-alloc priority formula floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/(death-birth) against them and found THE RULE PREDICTS THE CANDIDATE, NOT THE ROM -- ms has priority 1.50 against the table address's 0.25, so ms is allocated first and takes the lower register, which is exactly what default agbcc emits. That is not a source question and no spelling reaches it: it is the two allocators disagreeing, which is precisely what this file exists for. Byte-for-byte identical under old_agbcc with NOT ONE CHARACTER of the C changed. Consistent with the file's own note that old_agbcc is a strict superset across 0x0806F710-0x080745C0 and is the better first guess there, and with sub_08070BAC, whose park recorded the same 'value lands in r1 where agbcc puts it in r0' shape. Wave 60 also probed EVERY other non-asm-resident unmatched function in that span the same way and none of them moved; two got materially worse (sub_080723DC 88.3%->77.5%, sub_08073930 85.3% size-exact -> 14.7% at +8 bytes), so the region is NOT uniformly old_agbcc and this sweep should not be repeated. Each of the five is already its own single-function split unit, so gen_overrides_mk.py's one-function-per-.c constraint is satisfied with no file split.
